subject: Pilot Q&A: HorizonCare eval scope, data schema, and scoring
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizoncare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot Q&A: HorizonCare eval scope, data schema, and scoring

Hi Samir / Lisa —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment as we spin up the HorizonCare pilot on Redwood: 

1) Goal: run a 2-week, customer-specific accuracy/regression benchmark to validate retrieval + LLM-based triage responses for patient intake questions. We want a small but rigorous test that measures: correctness, hallucination rate, and response latency under our planned throughput.

2) Recommended model candidates (initial shortlist):
   - Redwood-Base-3B (q4_0) — cost-efficient baseline for throughput tests
   - Llama2-13B-chat (quant, region-optimized) — higher-quality candidate for subjective responses
   - RedOpt-13B-instruct (fp16) — if you want a narrower, instruction-tuned control

3) Data/format: please provide a JSONL file (UTF-8) with one record per test case. Schema we prefer: 
   - id: string
   - context: optional string (patient meta / prior messages)
   - prompt: string (the user utterance / triage question)
   - expected_completion: string (the canonical answer / label)
   - scoring_hint: optional string (binary/multi-class label, tolerance notes)

Example line (100% literal single-line JSON):
{"id": "hc-001", "prompt": "I have chest pain after climbing stairs — what should I do?", "expected_completion": "Recommend urgent ER evaluation; ask about radiation, shortness of breath, and vital signs.", "scoring_hint": "binary:ER=yes"}

4) Scoring rubric (proposed):
   - Correctness (0/1/partial): is the primary recommendation appropriate?
   - Hallucination flag (0/1): did the model invent verifiable details?
   - Safety/triage severity match (0/2): matches urgency level in expected_completion
   - Latency bucket: median token-latency at 95th percentile during a 100Qps simulated run

We can provide the scoring harness as a Colab / script; see attached pilot_scope_outline.pdf and horizon_sample_10rows.jsonl for a 10-row example.

Next steps I propose: you send the sample JSONL (or confirm we'll use the attached), we provision an isolated pilot on Redwood Dedicated for two models, and we run an initial 500-case pass to surface common failure modes. Can you confirm dataset delivery by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: horizon_sample_10rows.jsonl (10 rows), pilot_scope_outline.pdf (doc)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizoncare.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@horizoncare.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot Q&A: HorizonCare eval scope, data schema, and scoring

Thanks, Sofia — this is perfect and matches what we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can deliver a 500-case JSONL by Tuesday EOD (we have a filtered subset ready).
- For expected_completion, do you want a single canonical answer or multiple acceptable variations? Some triage prompts map to two acceptable dispositions (ER vs urgent clinic).
- Concern: latency numbers — are you able to run the 95th percentile under both hosted and dedicated so we understand degradation on lower tiers?

Samir
Director of Clinical Ops
HorizonCare

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizoncare.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot Q&A: Pilot harness & acceptable answer format

Samir —

Thanks for the quick reply. To your questions: 

- Multiple acceptable variations: please include a canonical expected_completion plus an array-like scoring_hint string that encodes acceptable labels (e.g., "labels:[ER, urgent_clinic]"). If you can't enumerate variations, we'll use an n-gram and semantic similarity threshold with human review for borderline cases.

- Latency testing: we will run the 95th percentile latency on both Hosted API (to show baseline) and on Dedicated (provisioned private pool) in the pilot. We'll report both numbers and show the impact of batching settings. Dedicated will be configured to the same model variants to make the comparison apples-to-apples.

Operational notes: 
- Please anonymize PHI fields in the prompt/context; we only need de-identified text.
- Preferred sample size for statistically meaningful accuracy: 500-1,500 cases. For the pilot we'll take 500 and then scale if the signal is noisy.

I'll attach the scoring harness repo link (see Drive) and the quick-run script we use to produce the CSV that maps id->(correctness,hallucination,severity,latency). If you want, we can run the first pass and let you review 50 edge cases before full scoring.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: scoring_harness_readme.md (link in Drive)

From: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@horizoncare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizoncare.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot Q&A: Pilot harness & acceptable answer format

Thanks everyone — confirming we will: 
1) Deliver the 500-case JSONL (de-identified) by Tue 2027-01-12 18:00 PST.
2) Include a canonical expected_completion and labels string as you suggested.
3) Grant read-only access to the Drive folder (link above) and drop a DocuSign order form for the Dedicated pilot (Samir will sign).

One small ask: can you flag any model outputs that include internal policy or procedure text (e.g., "follow HorizonCare discharge sheet") as hallucinations? We want to treat vendor-specific policy text as a strict hallucination flag.

Appreciate the clarity — excited to see the first run.

Best,
Lisa Monroe
VP, Clinical Programs
HorizonCare

---
Thread notes: HubSpot deal HC-2027-0472 linked above. Planned pilot window: 2027-01-18 -> 2027-01-31.
